frase_gancho.texto: Where Indigenous peoples live and how many languages they speak.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: You climb to the upper floor and the museum changes tense. Downstairs, everything was: pyramids, tombs, cities that no longer exist. Here, everything is. The upper floor is explored by theme, not by region, and this is the first hall: the one about places and languages. You will see a large map gathering the Indigenous peoples of Mexico, a house with its yard and its milpa, a mural that imagines the magical world of the Maya, and a painting from Xalitla, Guerrero, that tells the life of a town on amate paper. Notice one thing: each people speaks its own language, lives in its own territory, and tells in its own way where it stands.
